annotation_description: MiMo Johnny ended turn 1 with 8 cards in hand and no permanents on the battlefield, meaning they missed their land drop (Seat of the Synod) and failed to play any of their three 0-cost artifacts (Lotus Petal, 2x Mishra's Bauble). This forces a discard and puts them an entire turn behind. Playing Seat of the Synod + Lotus Petal + both Baubles would have set up a turn 2 Emry (with 3 artifacts reducing her cost to just U) or Patchwork Automaton with counters.

Attacking with Emry for 1 damage instead of using her tap ability to recast an artifact from the graveyard. The graveyard contains Lavaspur Boots and Mishra's Bauble, both of which could provide more value than 1 damage. With Metalcraft active (enabling Mox Opal), there was mana available to cast recovered artifacts.

Attacking with Emry for 1 damage (opponent at 19 life) means tapping Emry and forgoing her activated ability this turn. Emry could have tapped to let MiMo cast an artifact from the graveyard, such as Mishra's Bauble (free, provides card draw next upkeep and library information) or Lavaspur Boots ({1}, provides haste and ward for future creatures).

Warp-casting Pinnacle Emissary post-combat means it gets exiled at end step with no opportunity to generate tokens (no more artifact spells cast after it). Patchwork Automaton would be a permanent threat that grows over time and has ward 2.

Casting Kozilek's Command for X=1 uses all available mana on a modest effect (likely scry 1 + draw a card and one other minor mode) when the hand contains powerful 4-drops (Karn, The One Ring, Mystic Forge) that should be the priority. The stated reasoning about returning Expedition Map from graveyard is also completely wrong - Kozilek's Command cannot do that. The mana would be better saved or the turn used differently to set up casting a 4-drop next turn.

By casting Mishra's Bauble before Patchwork Automaton, MiMo Johnny misses a +1/+1 counter on the Automaton. Patchwork Automaton gets a counter whenever you cast an artifact spell, so casting it first (for 2 mana via Mox Opal + Seat of the Synod) and then casting the free Mishra's Bauble would have given the Automaton an immediate +1/+1 counter, making it a 2/2 instead of a 1/1.

Mishra's Bauble's activated ability lets you look at the top card of a target player's library. Targeting yourself is almost always better than targeting the opponent, because knowing what you'll draw next helps you plan your turns (especially with Emry decisions and whether to cast things from graveyard). Looking at the opponent's top card provides marginal information - you see one card they might draw but can't do anything about it. Looking at your own top card helps you sequence your plays optimally.

GLM47 Analyst had exactly enough mana to cast Tezzeret, Cruel Captain (costs {3}) by using the Candelabra + Voltaic Key untap chain to generate 3 colorless mana, but instead passed the turn doing nothing with a full hand of powerful spells.

MiMo Johnny already has Emry, Lurker of the Loch on the battlefield. Casting a second copy from hand will legend-rule one of them away, meaning they sacrifice the original Emry (which is already untapped and ready to use) just to get a fresh ETB mill trigger and a new summoning-sick Emry. While the mill is nice, they're wasting a card from hand for minimal benefit. Meanwhile, they have Patchwork Automaton (a 2-mana play that grows with artifact casts and has ward 2) or could set up Pinnacle Emissary via Warp for just U/R, both of which would develop the board without sacrificing an existing creature. Emry could also be used to activate her tap ability targeting Lavaspur Boots or Mishra's Bauble in the graveyard before being replaced, but casting the legend immediately wastes the existing copy's tap ability for this turn.

MiMo Johnny could have cast Kappa Cannoneer using Improvise by tapping Seat of the Synod for {U} and tapping 5 artifacts (Mox Opal, Urza's Bauble, 2 Drone Tokens, existing Patchwork Automaton) for the generic {5}. Kappa Cannoneer would enter as a 5/5 (gets +1/+1 counter from itself entering), be unblockable that turn, and have ward 4 making it very hard to remove. Instead they cast a 1/1 Patchwork Automaton and attacked for only 3.

MiMo Johnny declined to activate Emry, Lurker of the Loch, missing the line of targeting Lotus Petal in graveyard, casting it for free, then using Seat of the Synod ({U}) + Mox Opal ({C}) + Lotus Petal ({C}) + tapping 3 remaining artifacts for Improvise to cast Kappa Cannoneer (a 4/4 with ward 4 that would enter with a +1/+1 counter and be unblockable this turn). This would have dealt 5 damage and established a massive threat. Additionally, Urza's Bauble could have been sacrificed for free card advantage.

Attacking with the two Drone Tokens (0/1 creatures dealing 0 damage) taps them, preventing their use as Improvise sources for Kappa Cannoneer. With Seat of the Synod (U) + Mox Opal (1) + Urza's Bauble (Improvise) + 2 Drone Tokens (Improvise), MiMo Johnny could have exactly cast Kappa Cannoneer ({5}{U}) in the second main phase. Attacking with 0-power tokens for no damage gain cost the ability to deploy a powerful 4/4 ward 4 threat.

Mystic Forge is a powerful card advantage engine that would let the opponent (who has Urza lands generating lots of mana) chain artifacts and colorless spells from the top of their library, potentially finding The One Ring or other game-changing cards. Despite being ahead on board with the opponent at 9 life, letting this resolve risks the opponent stabilizing and overwhelming MiMo Johnny with card advantage.

At 1 life, activating The One Ring in response to its upkeep trigger adds a burden counter. When the upkeep trigger resolves, it counts burden counters at resolution time, meaning the added counter causes lethal damage. If there were 0 counters before, the trigger would have dealt 0 and they'd survive; now it deals 1 and they die.
